title: Localized ordinal suffixes, RTL ordering, and color-contrast fallbacks for dense timelines — prototype & review
creator: Marina Gómez
description:
Problem: Dense timeline cards in the Cost Explorer and Rollouts inspector render ordinal indicators (e.g., 1st, 2nd) next to short date/position labels. In some locales ordinal morphology differs (French '1er/1re', Spanish rarely uses suffixes, Japanese uses full-width numerals or particles), and in RTL layouts the visual placement of an inline suffix can break reading order or create confusing punctuation placement. Additionally, some color tokens used to surface timeline state fail WCAG contrast in dark mode when combined with dense graph overlays.

Goal: Define a design and ARIA strategy so ordinals are localized and readable for screen readers, visually placed correctly in LTR/RTL flows, and resilient to high-density truncation. Deliver a Figma prototype + HTML prototype that engineers can validate, with acceptance criteria and suggested fallback color tokens for contrast-safe rendering.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ordinal rendering strategy documented and implemented in prototype: canonical numeric value + locale-aware suffix generation, with suffixes optionally visually detached.
- ARIA pattern: the visible compact label can be aria-hidden with a separate aria-label that reads the localized full phrase (e.g., "Deployment 1er, 12 mars") so screen readers receive natural grammar.
- RTL behavior: visual ordering in RTL swaps suffix placement cleanly and punctuation is handled without orphaned characters.
- Keyboard nav: when focused via keyboard, timeline scrubber announces the localized long label in the console live-region.
- Contrast: provide two fallback color token pairs (high-contrast and color-blind-safe) that meet WCAG AA for normal text when over graph overlays and meet AAA for UI components where possible.
- Engineering checklist included: i18n keys, examples for CLDR-based ordinal rules, and an opt-in flag for locales that prefer spelled-out ordinals instead of suffixes.

Notes on approach: store timeline numeric index as a neutral source (e.g., "position: 1") and compute localized presentation at render time. For languages with gendered ordinals (e.g., French), consult localized grammatical context coming from the label resource; when grammatical context is unavailable, default to the most common form and track as an evaluation metric in QA.
acceptance_tests: Keyboard-only: Tab into timeline, press arrow keys to scrub; NVDA/VoiceOver should announce full localized label to the live region.
Screen reader: Verify aria-label reads a natural phrase in English, French, Arabic, Japanese, and Spanish test locales.
RTL visual: Switch to Arabic locale and ensure suffix placement and punctuation are not orphaned or visually detached from the number.
Contrast: Run automated color contrast audits across light/dark themes with graph overlays; verify tokens meet WCAG AA.
Unit tests: Locale fixtures for ordinal generation and UI snapshots for dense truncation cases.
design_decisions: Use aria-hidden on the compact visual span and provide a full aria-label on the container; this avoids adding extra DOM text for screen readers and keeps visuals compact.
For RTL locales, swap visual suffix placement but compute aria-label with natural language order from localization strings (not by reversing characters).
Provide a theme-level switch for 'High contrast / Color-blind safe' that maps to alternate tokens; engineers can use a single semantic token with CSS variables for fallback.
Avoid inserting Unicode ordinal markers directly in the display string for locales that require spelled-out words; opt into spelled-out form via locale metadata.
implementation_notes: Frontend: Add util in i18n layer that returns {presentation: string, ariaLabel: string} given numeric index + labelKey + locale. Reference CLDR rules where available.
Backend: Do NOT store localized suffixes. Keep canonical numeric index in events/telemetry to avoid language drift in historical data.
Accessibility: Use a polite live region for timeline announcements and rate-limit announcements when users scrub rapidly (debounce 250ms).
Engineering PR: see prototype PR #182 for HTML+JS sample and color token suggestions.
